extracted.intended_audience: journalism students, newspaper designers, and editors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and evaluating newspaper page makeup (balance, typography, headlines, and overall harmony) using newspaper pages and examples as illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony of the page
rubrics_metrics.description: Note the exquisite harmony of this page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall visual harmony is a criterion for good journalism page makeup; evaluate how well headlines, text blocks, images, and other elements work together to produce a coherent whole. The passage explicitly points to 'exquisite harmony' as a positive attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint in headlines (avoid sensationalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: The restraint exercised in headlines that the yellow journal would flaunt sensationally is a mark of good taste in journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines should avoid gratuitous sensationalism; tasteful, measured headline writing that resists 'yellow' (sensational) tendencies is considered good journalistic practice. Use headlines that inform rather than merely excite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and rhythm in layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Occult balance. Rhythm is achieved here through still another arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess page layout for balance and rhythmic flow — how the reader's eye moves across the page. Arrangement of elements (columns, story placement, image placement) should create a visual rhythm that guides reading and creates an even distribution of visual weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent use of typefaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The same type faces are used in all these plates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using consistent typefaces across related pages/plates contributes to visual harmony and readability. Evaluate typeface choices for consistency and appropriateness; avoid mixing disparate type styles that disrupt cohesion.
